Build the sparse inverse of the numerator relationship matrix (A-inverse)

Source: R/build_Ainv.R
build_Ainv.Rd

Constructs \(A^{-1}\) directly from a renumbered pedigree using the Henderson rules, without ever forming \(A\) explicitly. Individual inbreeding coefficients are computed internally via an ML92-style traversal.

build_Ainv(renum)

Arguments

renum

A data frame as returned by renum_pedigree(), with columns new_id, new_sire, and new_dam (integer, 0 = unknown).

Value

A list with:

Ainv

A sparse matrix of class dgCMatrix (N x N), the inverse of the numerator relationship matrix.

F

Numeric vector of length N with individual inbreeding coefficients.

Details

The pedigree must be in topological order (parents before offspring), as produced by renum_pedigree(). The heavy computations are delegated to compiled C++ code for efficiency with large pedigrees.

See also

renum_pedigree(), build_Ginv(), build_Hinv(), compute_connectedness()

Examples

ped <- data.frame(
  animal = c("A", "B", "C", "D"),
  sire   = c("0", "0", "A", "A"),
  dam    = c("0", "0", "B", "B")
)
renum <- renum_pedigree(ped, verbose = FALSE)
Ainv_res <- build_Ainv(renum)
Ainv_res$Ainv
#> 4 x 4 sparse Matrix of class "dgCMatrix"
#>                 
#> [1,]  2  1 -1 -1
#> [2,]  1  2 -1 -1
#> [3,] -1 -1  2  .
#> [4,] -1 -1  .  2
